slides.text: do pilates and lift? don't treat them as separate
save this. you'll need it at the gym
strength training helps your stability, control, muscular strength, and body endurance. it's not just building muscle, it's building a stronger body that moves smoother.
but the problem starts when you train with no plan. heavy legs or a hard upper session before pilates = you're walking into class gassed.

get a lifting plan that adjusts around your sport
try the app
keep heavy lifting days away from your intense pilates days. days close to pilates should be lighter. focused on movement and control.
squats, lunges, and pulling movements help a ton, just pick the right weight and keep your form clean.
the goal is for lifting to make you stronger for pilates, not heavier or less flexible.
